facts.claim: The physical chip contains two series-connected subarrays, each containing 118 parallel circular Hall elements; total element count is 236. Each subarray nominal resistance is R_K/236, about 109 ohm; the full series device is R_K/118, about 219 ohm.
Purchased epigraphene-on-SiC chips measured 7×7 mm with reported monolayer coverage above 95%. The array shares the chip with a separate rectangular Hall bar.

Source device geometry includes circular elements 150 micrometre diameter, superconducting NbN leads at least 120 nm thick and 50 micrometre wide, and two split contacts per element, each with six 15 micrometre prongs spaced 22 micrometres apart. These dimensions alone are not full CAD.

Preparation includes purchased epigraphene, lithographic definition, NbN edge-contact formation, a protective Pt layer, patterning, molecular doping and carrier-density tuning. These specialist fabrication categories are reviewed but no process recipe is supplied by this packet.
facts.evidence: MAIN p 7 Graphene growth and Fabrication methods

facts.claim: Array1 is described by source contacts I1–I0 and V1–V0; Array2 by I2–I0 and V2–V0. These source labels do not establish a qualified package pinout or switching command.

The main measurement platform uses a cryostat, superconducting magnet, local Cernox thermometer, electrical source/nanovoltmeter for initial characterization, and a cryogenic current comparator (CCC) for precision ratios. Source magnet 12 T and base 1.5 K are equipment specifications, not proposed robot setpoints or safety limits.

General electrical measurements occur around 2 K; precision CCC measurements are reported with the sample immersed in condensed helium at 2.1 K. Copper wiring leakage resistance is reported above 25 teraohm; this remains relevant to high-resistance comparison uncertainty.
Initial source/nanovoltmeter measurements have a reported noise level near 100 nV. A visually flat apparent plateau from this instrument is weaker evidence than a CCC quantization test.
facts.evidence: MAIN pp4,7; SI p1 S1; SI pp2–3 S2

facts.claim: The separate 200 micrometre-wide Hall bar supports longitudinal/transverse and contact checks. Reported density 1.7×10^11 cm^-2 and mobility 19600 cm² V^-1 s^-1 come from this Hall bar; subarray electronic properties are indirectly inferred, not directly measured by ordinary Hall geometry.
facts.evidence: MAIN p4 Fig3 and text; SI p1

facts.claim: Reported Hall-bar longitudinal resistance reaches the instrumental noise floor above roughly 3 T; no significant bias-related increase is reported up to 100 microampere. Residual Rxx for 5–100 microampere is 0.2±0.2 milliohm with k=2. Contact resistances below 2 ohm include about 1.5 ohm wiring.
SI S1 reports an NbN-contact transition near 12 K at 1 mA and a subarray magnetotransport plateau apparent above 3 T; a 4 milliohm/4 microvolt offset is assigned to voltmeter error.

The precision subarray comparison uses repeated CCC readings about 20 min each, each containing current-polarity changes to suppress thermal offsets/drift. A full measurement set has at least 45 readings; Fig 2 a example has 53. These are time-series readings on the device, not independent fabricated-chip repeats.
Fig 2 a/b labels use 3 mA and 2.1 K; Fig 2 c labels a 5 mA,5 T example. Fig 2 b shows field-dependent comparison around 4.5–5.5 T. Treat panel conditions separately.
facts.evidence: MAIN p3 Fig2 visual labels and caption

facts.claim: Source pooled subarray relative deviation is 0.033±0.082 nΩ/Ω; source practical single-set Allan-limited precision is about 0.2 nΩ/Ω. The two quantities represent different aggregation levels. Uncertainties default to k=1 unless otherwise stated.

The 100 ohm transfer standard is held in a temperature-controlled oil bath with known history. Main comparisons use 3 mA in this standard, approximately 23 microampere in the Hall bar or 2.75 mA in a subarray.
facts.evidence: MAIN p5 Fig4a,b and text; p7

facts.claim: Precision comparison configurations reported in Methods are array 1/array 2 winding 64/64, subarray/100 ohm 70/64, Hall bar/100 ohm 4130/32, and Hall bar/subarray 3776/32. Ratio labels do not specify terminal orientation, bridge residual correction or a command sequence.

The comparison network includes direct Array1↔Array2; each subarray↔100 ohm; Hall bar↔100 ohm; and direct Hall bar↔Array1. Indirect differences provide consistency checks but share underlying measurements.
facts.evidence: MAIN pp4–5 Fig4; SI p3 S3

facts.claim: Direct Hall-bar/subarray tests include positive and negative field directions at magnitudes 4.5,5.0,5.5 T. Fig 4 e x locations are offset for visibility and must not be digitized as exact commanded fields.
facts.evidence: MAIN p5 Fig4e caption and plot

facts.claim: The high-bias screen uses 5–10 CCC readings at each condition without Allan analysis; its error bars are standard deviations. Longer high-bias records have separate Allan analysis. Source explores bias up to 10 mA and reports field dependence at 8.5 mA.
facts.evidence: MAIN pp5–6 Fig5 caption and plot

facts.claim: At 8.5 mA the subarray comparison is field dependent; source reports deviation around 1 nΩ/Ω at 5 T and smaller apparent deviation below 5 T. This is a source outcome, not a universal safe-current or pass threshold.

Intentional nonquantizing tests include 3.6 T,3 mA,2.1 K. SI S2 reports direct relative deviation−0.0690±0.0006 microΩ/Ω and indirect−0.0730±0.0013 microΩ/Ω, and suggests one subarray departs earlier than the other. Their agreement statement requires the caution in C07.

A secondary 12.9 kiloohm room-temperature resistor in a controlled air bath is used for a high-bias common-mode check at subarray currents 3,5,8.5 mA. This test limits the possibility that both arrays deviate together far beyond their small difference.

The high-bias external-standard comparison reports pairwise expanded uncertainties 3.4,2.4,2.8 nΩ/Ω with k=2 for 3↔5,5↔8.5,3↔8.5 mA. The plotted absolute offset of that secondary standard is not the absolute error of a subarray.

Analysis uses inverse-variance weighted means, distinguishes standard deviations from standard deviations of means, and relies on a white-noise region of Allan deviation. Long-term drift/1/f noise limits useful averaging.
facts.evidence: MAIN p7 Data analysis Eq1–4; pp3,5–6

facts.claim: Table 1 contains 9 literature/current-work rows. Seven literature rows are context only and were not separately source-reviewed. The final two rows describe this work at 5 mA/5 T and 8.5 mA/4.25 T, both 2.1 K.

Discussion proposes future non-unity, redundant array configurations and interlaboratory comparisons. These were not performed experiments in this paper. A Kibble balance/ampere realization is a motivation, not a demonstrated branch.

All raw data are available only on request according to the paper. This review does not audit numerical raw readings, calibration logs, exact sweep schedules, bridge configuration files or original analysis code.
